:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right]
$$

 

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$ on $A?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Which elementary row operation could transform the matrix $A$ into the matrix $B$, where 

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has been changed is the $2$nd row. 

Now, applying the operation $R_2:=R_2+1 \cdot R_1,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4+1\cdot (-4) & 1+1\cdot (-2) & 2+1\cdot 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the transformation could be done by the operation 

$$
R_2:=R_2+1\cdot R_1
$$

or simply

$$
R_2:=R_2+R_1.
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Given that

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}
$$

 which elementary row operation could make $a_{22}=0?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
In the given matrix, we have $a_{22}=5$ and we want to perform an elementary row operation that makes $a_{22}=0.$

- We *cannot* make $a_{22}=0$ by switching two rows, because there are no rows with $0$ as the second entry.

- We *cannot* multiply the second row by $0,$ because we are only allowed to multiply rows by *nonzero* constants.

- However, we *can* add a multiple of another row to the $2$nd row to make $a_{22}=0.$

Looking at the first row, we see that $a_{12}=1.$ If we add $-5$ times this entry to $a_{22},$ we will get $a_{22}=0$ as desired. So, the elementary row operation that we need to use is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1.
$$

Applying this operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1+(-5)\cdot 3 & 5+(-5)\cdot 1 & 6+(-5)\cdot (-2) \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -16 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the desired elemetary row operation is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1,
$$

or simply

$$
R_2 := R_2 -5 R_1.
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
Suppose we are given a system of linear equations and its respective augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3} &=-2 \\ 5{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

We can apply some operations to the augmented matrix that do not change the set of solutions for the corresponding system. These operations are called **elementary row operations**. 

After applying an **elementary row operation** to the augmented matrix, the new corresponding system will have the same solutions.

There are three types of elementary row operations:

- switching any two rows: 

$$
R_i \leftrightarrow R_j
$$

- multiplying (each element of) a row by a non-zero number: 

$$
R_i := k R_i,\qquad k \neq 0
$$

- adding a multiple of one row to another row: 

$$
R_j := R_j+k R_i,\qquad j \neq i
$$

In the notations above, the "$:=$" symbol is called the **assignment operator.** We use this to assign new values to every element of a given row.

For example, the row operation $R_1 := 2 R_1$ means, "create a new row $1$ by taking the old row $1$ and multiplying it by $2.$" When we do this, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 4 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]\,{R}_{1}:=2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2\cdot 1 & 2\cdot 3 & 2\cdot (-1) & 2\cdot 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 4 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & 6 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 4 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

A few final points on notation.

- We use the similarity symbol ($\sim$) to indicate when one matrix is transformed into another matrix using elementary row operations.

- The assignment operator $:=$ is sometimes called the "walrus operator" because it looks like a walrus on its side!

 which elementary row operation could make $a_{22}=0?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
In the given matrix, we have $a_{22}=5$ and we want to perform an elementary row operation that makes $a_{22}=0.$

- We *cannot* make $a_{22}=0$ by switching two rows, because there are no rows with $0$ as the second entry.

- We *cannot* multiply the second row by $0,$ because we are only allowed to multiply rows by *nonzero* constants.

- However, we *can* add a multiple of another row to the $2$nd row to make $a_{22}=0.$

Looking at the first row, we see that $a_{12}=1.$ If we add $-5$ times this entry to $a_{22},$ we will get $a_{22}=0$ as desired. So, the elementary row operation that we need to use is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1.
$$

Applying this operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1+(-5)\cdot 3 & 5+(-5)\cdot 1 & 6+(-5)\cdot (-2) \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -16 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the desired elemetary row operation is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1,
$$

or simply

$$
R_2 := R_2 -5 R_1.
$$

:step/content.:knowledge-point/title: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What is the coefficient matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=1 \\ 2y &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=1 \\ 0x+2y &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
		1 & -2  \\
		0 & 2 
	\end{bmatrix}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Coefficient Matrix of a System of Linear Equations

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y+x-5-3z &=0 \\ z &=y+7x \\ y+3-2z &=1-2x\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $x,y,z$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y-3z &=5 \\ -7x-y+z &=0 \\ 2x+y-2z &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
		1 & 1 & -3  \\
		-7 & -1 & 1  \\
                2 & 1 & -2 
	\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix  is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -3 & 5 \\ -7 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Augmented Matrix of a System of Linear Equations

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What would be the system of equations for the following augmented matrix?

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}5 & -4 & -12 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix consists of two parts: the coefficient matrix and the column of constants.

The coefficient matrix represents the coefficients in the linear system, while the column of constants represents the constants on the right-hand sides of the equations.

Using the variables $x$ and $y,$ then, the corresponding system of equations is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}5x-4y &=-12 \\ 3x+y &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the System of Equations Associated With an Augmented Matrix

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}\frac{c}{2} &=a \\ 5+3b-a &=4c \\ d &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $a,b,c,d$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-a+0b+\frac{1}{2}c+0d &=0 \\ -a+3b-4c+0d &=-5 \\ 0a+0b+0c+d &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$
